evals.prompt: I'm starting a small C library for parsing a line-based config format, plus a CLI that uses it, and later maybe a tiny HTTP service. Team of two, we develop on Macs, deploy to Linux. Current plan: a hand-written Makefile with CFLAGS=-O2 -g, gnu99, headers in src/, no tests yet, and we'd copy the binary to the server with scp. What should the setup look like?
evals.expected_output: An opinionated setup: C23 strict (C_STANDARD 23, extensions off; public headers C11-compatible), CMake >= 3.25 with CMakePresets.json (dev/asan/tsan/release/ci) and Ninja, target-only flags on INTERFACE policy targets, include/<name>/ public headers with an opaque type and documented ownership, a status-enum + out-param API, tests via a tiny test.h + CTest, ASan+UBSan in CI with -Werror from a preset, probed OpenSSF hardening in release, a libFuzzer target for the parser, clang-format/clang-tidy, and deploy as a static musl binary (Alpine or zig cc cross-compile) on distroless/static with Kamal behind Cloudflare instead of scp. Mentions macOS-specific gotchas (no libFuzzer in Apple clang, ld64 rejects -z flags, threads.h missing). Gives first commands (e.g. scripts/new_project.py or cmake --workflow --preset ci).
assertions: Recommends CMake with presets (dev/asan/release or similar) instead of the hand-written Makefile, using target_* commands rather than global CFLAGS
Recommends C23 (or at least C17) instead of gnu99, and keeps the public header compatible with older standards or explains the choice
Proposes an include/<name>/ public header with an opaque type and documented ownership (who frees)
Recommends a status-code error convention with out-parameters rather than printing or sentinel returns
Adds tests run by CTest and a sanitizer (ASan/UBSan) build in CI
Recommends hardening flags for release (e.g. _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, stack protector, PIE, RELRO) and notes they must be probed or platform-guarded because macOS ld64/arm64 reject some
Recommends fuzzing the parser (libFuzzer) and notes Apple clang lacks libFuzzer or suggests Linux CI for it
Replaces scp with a reproducible deploy: static (musl) binary in a minimal container (distroless/scratch), ideally Kamal

evals.prompt: Review our C project at evals/files/flawed_project and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review. Critical: gets() and unbounded scanf("%s"); strcpy/strcat/sprintf into fixed buffers; printf(name)/printf(desc) format-string bugs; config_describe returns a pointer to a stack array; config_free frees cfg then reads cfg->items (use-after-free); system() with a config-controlled hook (shell injection). High: malloc results unchecked; cfg->items = realloc(cfg->items, ...) leaks on failure and its size multiplication can overflow; atoi on a possibly NULL value; assert(port = 8080) is an assignment that vanishes under NDEBUG; volatile int as a thread flag (data race; use atomic_bool); void main; rand() for a session token. Medium/low: CMake 3.0 minimum fails on CMake 4; global CMAKE_C_FLAGS/include_directories/add_definitions and hard-coded -Werror; no warnings, hardening, tests, or sanitizers; file(GLOB); no C standard; missing include guard and config_load() empty parameter list; <threads.h> not on macOS; strtok; strlen in loop; ubuntu runtime image as root. Concrete fixes, ending with the top three.
assertions: Flags gets() and scanf("%s") without width as buffer overflows and recommends fgets / a field width
Flags strcpy/strcat/sprintf and recommends snprintf with a checked return (or memcpy with a length check)
Flags printf(name) / printf(desc) as format-string vulnerabilities
Flags config_describe returning a pointer to a local (stack) array
Flags the use-after-free in config_free (free(cfg) before free(cfg->items))
Flags unchecked malloc and the p = realloc(p, ...) leak pattern (and/or the unchecked size multiplication)
Flags system() with config-controlled input as command injection
Flags assert(port = 8080) (assignment / side effect removed by NDEBUG) or atoi without error checking
Flags volatile used as a cross-thread flag and recommends <stdatomic.h>
Flags the CMake issues: minimum version 3.0 fails on CMake 4, global flags, no warnings/hardening/tests
Orders findings by severity

evals.prompt: Our CI builds with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` and all tests pass, but a customer hit a signed integer overflow in production that UBSan should have caught. Our CMake adds these to every build: -O2 -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 -fstack-protector-strong -fno-strict-overflow -fcf-protection=full -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now. Also the macOS developers say the build is broken on their M-series laptops. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses: -fno-strict-overflow (like -fwrapv) makes signed overflow defined, so UBSan's signed-integer-overflow check is silenced; drop it from sanitizer builds. Also UBSan needs -fno-sanitize-recover=all or it only prints and tests pass. _FORTIFY_SOURCE conflicts with ASan and should be limited to optimized non-sanitizer builds (with -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE first). On Apple Silicon: -fcf-protection is x86-only (error on arm64; use -mbranch-protection=standard on AArch64) and ld64 rejects -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now. Fix: move flags to INTERFACE targets, probe each with check_c_compiler_flag (under -Werror) / check_linker_flag, separate asan/release presets. Gives the CMake snippet.
assertions: Identifies -fno-strict-overflow (defined wrapping) as the reason UBSan did not report the signed overflow, and removes it from sanitizer builds
Mentions -fno-sanitize-recover (UBSan otherwise continues and tests pass) or an equivalent halt-on-error setting
Notes _FORTIFY_SOURCE should not be combined with ASan builds (or only applied to optimized non-sanitizer builds)
Explains -fcf-protection is x86-only and fails on arm64 (suggests -mbranch-protection=standard for AArch64)
Explains macOS ld64 rejects -Wl,-z,relro/now
Recommends probing flags (check_c_compiler_flag/check_linker_flag or generator expressions) on target-scoped INTERFACE targets instead of global flags, with separate sanitizer and release presets

evals.prompt: Write me a small C module for a fixed-capacity ring buffer of bytes that multiple producer threads and one consumer thread will use in our service. Include the header, implementation, and tests.
evals.expected_output: A prefixed module (ringbuf_*) with an opaque type in include/ringbuf/ringbuf.h, ownership documented (create/destroy, caller owns), status enum returned with [[nodiscard]]-style annotation and out-params written only on success, capacity validated with checked arithmetic, a mutex + condition variables (pthreads) for multi-producer access (or a clearly justified atomic design), thread-safety documented in the header, no volatile, bounded memcpy, NULL-safe destroy, and tests using a tiny assert harness registered with CTest including a multi-threaded producer/consumer test meant to run under TSan, plus the CMake target wiring with Threads::Threads.
assertions: Uses an opaque type with a name prefix and paired create/destroy (destroy NULL-safe) with ownership documented in the header
Returns status codes (enum) with out-parameters rather than printing or returning magic values
Uses pthread mutex/condition variables or C11 atomics correctly for multiple producers; does not use volatile for synchronization
Documents the thread-safety contract in the header
Checks allocation results and guards size arithmetic against overflow
Includes tests (a minimal harness or framework) with a concurrent producer/consumer test and mentions running it under ThreadSanitizer
Shows CMake wiring (target_link_libraries with Threads::Threads, add_test) rather than global flags
